How to read the dates. This archive is two archives wearing one schema. The 10,478 legacy files carry no links and no read events: their date is the publication date parsed out of a filename, so a quarter before 2012 says when the writing appeared, not when it was read. The 5,903 Instapaper and Matter articles from 2012 on carry real save and archive dates. Two thirds of the corpus, 10,672 articles, is dated by that proxy. Every strip and step runs on one shared axis of quarters from 2005 Q1 to 2026 Q3, and the amber lines are the average of each era, annotated with their value. There is no time of day anywhere in this archive, so nothing here is drawn by hour.

Three decisions

The cover is drawn. What is not settled is where it lives, which number leads each column, and whether the two covers already shipped should move.

  • Decision 1 · where it lives
    Cover as the home page with the weeks index below it, or a separate /cover/?
    Recommend: cover as home, index below, one page. Books and viewing both put the cover at the root, and a reader arriving from either sibling expects the same shape. A separate /cover/ would be a second entrance that neither sibling has, and the sticky bar has nowhere to point at it. The catch is the measure. The cover wants 1,180 pixels and four columns; the current index is a 720-pixel single column, which is why the frame below sits narrower than the cover above it. Stacking them means one page with two measures, or widening the index to match. Widening is the larger change and can wait.
  • Decision 2 · the hero per column
    Are these the four numbers, and is Articles the right amber one?
    Articles carries the amber because 16,382 is the number the whole archive is about, and it is already the first anchor number on the live page. The other three are deliberately not totals: 827 is the writing, 1,164 is the reach, and 14.8% is the only hero that is a share rather than a count, because the subject column has no honest total. Swapping any of the three is cheap.
  • Decision 3 · the AI hero
    Is "artificial intelligence, 14.8% since 2018" too on the nose?
    It is the largest real movement in the vocabulary, up 14.1 points against the pre-2012 era while mobile devices and social media each fell about six. The alternative hero is the vocabulary itself, 248 curated entries over 80.8% of the corpus, which is a fact about the pipeline rather than about the reading. Adam's call.
  • Decision 4 · the siblings
    Do books and viewing need any change once this ships?
    Recommend: no change to either. This cover was built to their anatomy, not the reverse. One small drift is worth noting: their sticky bars carry a second row of page links because each has four pages, and reading has one page plus its year anchors. That asymmetry is already documented in the reading site's own nav helper and should stay.
